Dead & Company website

The band’s site after its 2026 Golden Gate Park shows: fat, outlined concert-poster lettering and a stippled drawing on full-bleed yellow.

Source
deadandcompany.com
Creator
Dead & Company
Style

Moods

Evidence
Captured with tools/capture.mjs (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Third-party work, stored with credit for commentary. License: unverified. Rights policy

Observed

  • A saturated golden yellow fills the whole viewport.
  • DEAD & COMPANY is centered at the top in very fat, tight capitals filled with pink, with a black outline and a black offset shadow.
  • GOLDEN GATE PARK sits below in tall condensed capitals filled with light blue and outlined in black, with an offset black shadow.
  • Smaller lines, CELEBRATING 60 YEARS OF THE GRATEFUL DEAD’S MUSIC and SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA, are in a wide black geometric sans.
  • A stippled drawing of the Golden Gate Bridge in light blue, green, and black, with a DEADCO blimp, fills the lower half.
  • The navigation at top right is plain black text and social icons.

Why it belongs

The page borrows the poster tradition of its own subject, the Grateful Dead, through lettering and a colored ground. It stops short of the style’s distortion and ornament.

Measured values: color.chromaticShare 0.73 and type.centerShare 1.0 pass; color.hues is 2, surface.radius.median is 0, and color.patternShare is 0, because the stipple is an image.

Borrow

Give display lettering a fill color, a black outline, and an offset black shadow for a poster look that stays legible.

Use a saturated yellow as the page ground instead of white.
